findings.description: setYieldStrategy (V2:249, V1:257) and finalizeAndReset (V2:673) are the only state-mutating entry points lacking nonReentrant. setYieldStrategy makes external calls into the old strategy (_routeExit -> relinquishPrincipal/withdraw) and the new one (strategy.deposit) around writing yieldStrategy[token]. Not exploitable as written: the require(totalStaked == 0) gate makes the _routeExit branch unreachable and the strategy is owner-wired. Hardening/consistency note.

Per-user require()s inside the migrateIn slice loop ('top-up surplus exhausted' at :281, 'par not restored' at :294) revert the whole owner batch, and the shared surplus budget is consumed in slice order so earlier users can starve later ones. Self-limiting: migrateIn is paginated (start,end) and users can self-rescue via the permissionless claimTimedOut hatch. Ordering-dependence of the surplus budget is for econ-scanner.

CrossVersionMigrator.migrate calls newStaker.depositFor in a loop with no userInfo snapshot and no shortfall gross-up, unlike InPlaceMigrator._reinjectWithTopup which exists precisely to close that gap (ss12m1/M-07 fix). If the destination staker haircuts the credit, the migrated user is silently underpaid. migrate also lacks nonReentrant. LEAD ONLY: whether the destination can credit less than it pulls depends on destination yield-strategy wiring, which SAST cannot settle. Route to code-scanner/econ-scanner.
